newsitem.title: UK: Plasmon off nearly 45 pct on profits warning.
newsitem.headline: Plasmon off nearly 45 pct on profits warning.

text.p: Shares in CD and computer tape backup maker Plasmon Plc fell by almost 45 percent on Wednesday after the company issued a profits warning.
Its share price was down 80 pence at 99 pence at 1025 GMT.
"Due to the difficult start to the year we expect to make a significant loss in the first half compared with a profit of 0.4 million stg in the same period last," the company said in a statement.

It said sales in the first quarter to June 30 were four percent below the same period last year, while weak market conditions together with the strength of sterling led to a 16 percent fall in European sales compared with last year.
Sales in the United States, however, were up 17 percent as a result of a contract with IBM Corp in May 1996.
The sales performance for the whole group was also affected by "delays and quality product issues" from suppliers of CD-R and MO drives.

Excess manufacturing capacity and inventory led to tough conditions in the CD-R disc market with price declines in the first quarter much more than expected, putting pressure on the profitability of the group's CD-R business.

"We have delayed the delivery of the next four production lines while we re-engineer our manufacturing operations to ensure that we have the cost base and product specification to be competitive in the world market," the group added.

Despite the profits warning, Plasmon expects an improvement in the second half -- traditionally its stronger half -- helped by a contribution from a new contract to make tape libraries, deliveries for which began in the second quarter.
